title: An experimental pathway towards an exact theory of strong coupling
abstract: We employ a mathematically equivalent form of the GKLS master equation to arrive at an exact theoretical description of a two-level system strongly coupled to the environment. The framework, while intuitive, shedding light on the physics of the problem, and agreeing with existing results, such as thermalisation to a non-canonical state, is based around three parameters that are unknown outside of the weak coupling regime -- the analogue to the detailed balance relation, and two coupling strength constants. As a way forward, we propose a feasible experimental protocol based on a solid-state electronic quantum dot device, through which the fundamental parameters of the problem can be revealed, which would further the fundamental understanding of strong coupling.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of modeling strong coupling in open quantum systems using a generalized GKLS master equation. It derives an exact theoretical description based on three key parameters ($\gamma, \Gamma, \phi$) and proposes a concrete experimental measurement scheme utilizing a solid-state quantum dot to determine these fundamental physical constants.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an exact theoretical description of strong coupling effects in open quantum systems, where standard master equation approaches fail.
main_result: They propose a feasible experimental protocol using a solid-state quantum dot to measure the fundamental parameters ($\gamma, \Gamma, \phi$) governing this strongly coupled regime.
method: The theory is built upon generalizing the GKLS master equation and analyzing its stationary state solutions in a specific basis derived from the system Hamiltonian and charge operator.
model_or_system: The model is a two-level system (quantum dot) strongly coupled to an electron bath. The dynamics are governed by a generalized GKLS master equation, analyzed using parameters related to coupling strengths ($\Gamma$) and detailed balance analogues ($\gamma$).
key_observables: The expectation value of the number operator, $\langle\hat{N}angle$, is the primary measurable observable used in the proposed experimental protocol.
important_parameters: Three key parameters are identified: $\gamma$ (analogue to detailed balance), $\Gamma$ (effective coupling strength), and $\phi$ (related to the Hamiltonian basis).
main_assumptions: The framework relies on purely algebraic manipulations of the GKLS equation, and a major practical assumption is the ability to implement strong projecting measurements in the quantum dot.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates how the mean population ($\langle\hat{N}angle$) changes when subjected to controlled dephasing noise applied either to the number operator ($ eta_N$) or the Hamiltonian ($ eta_H$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by generalizing the GKLS equation for strong coupling. It then details how this theory maps onto a physical quantum dot setup, outlining specific measurement protocols using QPC sensing to extract the three unknown parameters.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics and thermalization in strongly coupled open systems, which is central to modern quantum thermodynamics and mesoscopic physics.

FIG. 2. A sample dependence of mean population in the presence of external dephasing in ˆ N and ˆH as a function of noise intensity, Γext, standing for ΓN or ΓH. In the case plotted, Γ = 0.4, φ = 0.2.

Figure 2 shows the dependence of the mean population of the quantum dot, βN and βH as a function of the ex- ternal dephasing strength ΓN or ΓH, shown as Γext. In the weak noise regime the dephasing in ˆN, as expected, leads to a lower mean population, while the dephasing in ˆH increases it. The latter is due to the fact that de- phasing destroys the components of the density matrix orthogonal to the dephasing operator, which, in the case of ˆH are i[ ˆH, ˆN] and −sin φ ˆN + cos φ ˆD. The negative sign in ˆN in the second vector leads to a restoration of mean population.
